namespace OuterMeasure

/-- `OuterMeasure.pi m` is the finite product of the outer measures `{m i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be the maximal outer measure `n` with the property that
  `n (pi univ s) ≤ ∏ i, m i (s i)`, where `pi univ s` is the product of the sets
  `{s i | i : ι}`. -/
protected def pi (m : ∀ i, OuterMeasure (α i)) : OuterMeasure (∀ i, α i) :=
  boundedBy (piPremeasure m)

/-- `Measure.pi μ` is the finite product of the measures `{μ i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be measure corresponding to `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi`. -/
protected irreducible_def pi : Measure (∀ i, α i) :=
  toMeasure (OuterMeasure.pi fun i => (μ i).toOuterMeasure) (pi_caratheodory μ)

definition_kinds.meaning: D has d real coordinates; E has q+1 real coordinates. Row squared norm is the Euclidean sum of coordinate squares.
An outcome is a tuple of q+1 column vectors in D. It is not a single canonical row variable. No Gaussian law on the function carrier Omega is asserted.

Measure.pi of the actual standard Gaussian measures on D. Thus the q+1 columns follow the source independent standard d-Gaussian experiment. The actual product-probability and factor sigma-finiteness instances were synthesized, not taken as new inputs.
The a-th coordinate is column a at physical coordinate i, rewrapped by WithLp.toLp2 into Euclidean row space. Source indices are i.val+1 and a.val+1.
Both fields are conclusions: Measurable(row i) and Measure.map(row i)mu=stdGaussian E. This structure is not an assumption bundle.
L=2(q+1)+3log(1000d). All rows use the same outcome omega and the closed condition norm(row i omega)^2<=L. The complement is the strict any-bad event with norm squared>L.
The positive real rational999/1000 is embedded into nonnegative extended reals. It is exactly the source0.999, with no change of normalization.

scope: Concrete original-column product experiment, marginal-law transport and global all-good event. No inference of full joint-row independence from marginal laws.
